title: xDrip+ draining G5 transmitter batter
body:
Hello, I've been using xDrip+ for over a year but started having trouble with transmitter battery lately. I was using a Galaxy S5 and a G5 transmitter and got decent usage out of it. However, my phone broke about a month ago so I had to start using a BLU Dash X2 and the transmitter voltage and resistance has been degrading quite rapidly. My original transmitter gave out right after switching to the BLU. A replacement only lasted 3 weeks and another replacement gave me a low battery warning after 24 days. I'm not in native mode and have unchecked all additional Bluetooth settings except OB1, which has to be enabled for me to get any data. Do I need to get a new phone and is there a certain setting that maximizes battery life? Also, I'm thinking of switching back to the G4 and having the transmitter send the data, so will the G4 work with xDrip+? Here is my current System Status using a brand new transmitter from the beginning of December:


![49202804_517287285432269_2069196749360070656_n](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40383153/50805049-aaca9480-12be-11e9-9f54-a030841b24b1.png)

comments.body:
G4 works fine with xDrip+, but you need to build a bridge (xBridge,
wixel-xdrip, xBridge+), as the G4 is NOT native Bluetooth.
Been using G4 for years, even on the original xDrip, which is what started
it all.
Cheers

What is the factory date on your transmitter box? Running in non-native mode I would expect to use the least battery of all as the transmitter doesn't have to do any calculations.

Please see #566 

I'm noticing that not using G5 Native mode seems to lead to early transmitter death.

I tried putting the current transmitter in Native mode but it didn't connect, so I had to turn it off. The transmitter is newly manufactured. The only things I can think of is either the phone is of poor quality, causing the connection to continually drop and reconnect or the sensors might be drawing more battery from the transmitter. Because I can get a few weeks from one sensor, I have a number of them that are old and expired. They perform perfectly well even if they are over a year old, but they might not connect as well. I used the G4 kit with the transmitter with this phone and got great usage from the transmitters. The current battery level is: 267 for A, 255 for B and 785 for the resistance. I'm sure any day now it will give out on me.

If you tried to enable Native mode after the transmitter battery was already low, I'm pretty sure the G5 will refuse.  You'd have to enable native mode when the transmitter is relatively new.

The age of the sensors really shouldn't mater.  I have a bunch of expired sensors that work perfectly well.

The phone trying to re-connect also shouldn't really matter, though who knows.

After Native mode stops working on my current transmitter (another few weeks or so, assuming it cuts off after three months) I'll switch back to non-native OB1.  If the transmitter only lasts less than a month after that, I'll have to assume it's something with the way xDrip communicates in OB1 mode that's killing the transmitter.   If it goes longer than another month, then I'll have to assume that the transmitter requires getting native mode up and running first, else it gets stuck in some power sucking mode.  

My current transmitter is about 2 1/2 months in, and voltage a/b/r is 315/304/638.  On the two previous transmitters that I did not enable native mode on, voltage dropped below 300 before it was a month old. 

Apart from the communication and battery issues, I prefer xDrip's non-native mode.  It seems to be far more accurate and requires less calibration than G5's native mode.

I got used G5 transmitter as a gift and hat to replace batteries 4 times up to now.
I noticed that:
- Resistance is always high 
- Batteries voltage is ~3.05V up to day 6 or 7 and then I have sudden drop to ~2.6-2.8V
- Up to day 10 or 11, transmitter is ready for new batteries
If I have to guess, I would say that 'preemptive restart' has something with sudden battery drain.

I got new transmitter and Sony, Duracell and Energizer batteries so I want to see what will happen to new and never used transmitter and different type of batteries. Right now, I'm on 7.8th day of Old transmitter.

I got 'Authenticate G5 before each read' unchecked by mistake up to day 5. After voltage drop I uncheck it again. I might be a bit superstitious here.

If anyone wants to look at the issue or need some further info, please free to contact me.

Thanks!

OK, I lost hope and got one unused G5 over ebay so I didn't update. It is empty now :(
Now, I believe that I found what causes battery drainage and how to deal with it. It's not ultimate solution but it will help save you grinding epoxy and wasting batteries...

First settings (If not written, it was OFF):
- Use the OB1 - ON
- Native Algorithm - ON
- Preemptive restarts - ON (there was one restart on day 3 or 6, can't recall)
- Allow OB1 unbonding - ON
- Allow OB1 initiate bonding -ON

On end of the day 9th (3h before if you look at sensor insertion) of using battery replaced G5 and sensor, I noticed that xdrip started to report 'sensor errors'. It was strange. Logs from 'View events log' showed no entries. I had left it for half an hour and then I thought that **it might be that Sensor stopped as day 9th had passed**! The time when non hacked sensor will expire (g5 marks it as expired). But, it was restarted on day 6!? So, it was 3 day old session!
I stopped sensor and started it again, waited 2h warm up time and it worked. Voltages the same. 
Tomorrow, at the same time, same problem. 'Sensor errors'. I waited for an almost hour, stopped it an noticed strange stoppage time: **2020-02-11 01:13:46 while it was 2020-01-30 23:57**
So, I give 'hard reset transmitter' command, started sensor, waited for 2h warmup time and 21h had passed. On 1st site, it's OK. Voltages are OK (lost only 0.01V yesterday on 1hour 'sensor error' time.

I suggest this path TO MITIGATE PROBLEM (if you have battery drainage) until fix:
- turn Preemptive restarts OFF
- day 9 (or earlier if more convenient): stop sensor, hard reset transmitter*, start sensor again
* I'm not sure whether to hard reset transmitter but I hadn't time to check. So, if anyone in control can try to do stop-start sensor prior 'sensor errors' without hard resetting transmiter and it works after 28 hours, please comment!

@edmundac I would like us to close this issue unless you believe there is still an issue with xDrip.
People use xDrip with G5 and G6 all over the world.  
It happens a lot when a transmitter is shipped with a faulty battery.  When that happens, it doesn't matter if you use xDrip or the Dexcom receiver, the transmitter will fail in a few days.

The only way one can prove that xDrip causes extra battery drain is to do a comparison.  If one had a transmitter with rechargeable batteries, he could charge fully and then use the transmitter with xDrip for say one month and monitor the voltage on a daily basis.
Then, charge the battery again and use it again for a month but this time with the Dexcom app and measure the battery voltage after.  If the voltage after is lower when using xDrip, that will prove that xDrip drains more.

Without such a test, all we have is speculation.
